cards.explanation: The answer is forsake. The text says it plainly: "Thus they forsook the LORD and did not serve Him." (Judges 10:6) To forsake is to walk away and leave Him behind. Israel had a whole crowd of gods to serve, friends, and the LORD was the One they left out.

The answer is the Philistines and Ammonites. The text says He "…sold them into the hands of the Philistines and Ammonites…" (Judges 10:7) These were neighboring nations. The LORD's anger burned, and these two were the hands Israel landed in.

The answer is eighteen. The Philistines and Ammonites "…harassed and oppressed the Israelites, and they did so for eighteen years…" (Judges 10:8) That's a long stretch, friends. Eighteen years of waiting makes a person count every single one.

The answer is cry out. The text says, "Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD…" (Judges 10:10) Israel was in deep distress, and the cry went up to the LORD. Sometimes that's all a person has left, and it's enough to start with.

The answer is False. Listen to the question the LORD asks: "…you cried out to Me, did I not save you from their hands?" (Judges 10:12) He's looking back at the Egyptians, Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines, Sidonians, Amalekites and Maonites. When Israel cried out then, the answer was a rescue, friends, not a leave-behind.

The answer is no longer. The LORD says, "But you have forsaken Me and served other gods, so I will no longer save you." (Judges 10:13) That's a heavy line. I'm not going to hurry past it, friends, because it's a serious moment.

The answer is that they ask Him to deliver them today. They say it right out loud: "Deal with us as You see fit; but please deliver us today!" (Judges 10:15) They repeat their confession and put themselves in His hands. Then comes the ask for today. When you've been waiting a long time, I think you stop asking for later.

The answer is that they put the foreign gods away and serve the LORD. The text says, "So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD…" (Judges 10:16) Their words were followed by action. The gods that had been sitting among them were put away.

The answer is True. After they put away the foreign gods and served the LORD, "…He could no longer bear the misery of Israel." (Judges 10:16) That's a tender line, friends, and I think it's worth reading twice. The text puts the LORD's response right after their turn back to Him.

The answer is head of all who live in Gilead. The rulers of Gilead tell one another, "Whoever will launch the attack against the Ammonites will be the head of all who live in Gilead." (Judges 10:18) The verse before says the Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead, and the Israelites camped at Mizpah. So the offer is leadership for whoever steps up first.
